title: Parse JSON data
instruction: Define a function `parse_people(json_data)` that takes a JSON string (an array of objects with "name" and "city" keys) and returns a string where each person is formatted as `[name] lives in [city]`, one per line.
test_suite:
import json

def test_two_people():
    data = '[{"name": "Alice", "city": "New York"}, {"name": "Bob", "city": "London"}]'
    result = exercise.parse_people(data)
    assert result == "Alice lives in New York\nBob lives in London", f"Expected 2 people, got {result!r}"

def test_single_person():
    data = '[{"name": "Charlie", "city": "Tokyo"}]'
    result = exercise.parse_people(data)
    assert result == "Charlie lives in Tokyo", f"Expected single person, got {result!r}"

def test_empty_array():
    data = '[]'
    result = exercise.parse_people(data)
    assert result == "", f"Expected empty string, got {result!r}"

def test_three_people():
    data = '[{"name": "Diana", "city": "Paris"}, {"name": "Eve", "city": "Berlin"}, {"name": "Frank", "city": "Sydney"}]'
    result = exercise.parse_people(data)
    assert result == "Diana lives in Paris\nEve lives in Berlin\nFrank lives in Sydney", f"Expected 3 people, got {result!r}"

title: Write friends list to JSON
instruction: Define a function `friends_to_json(friends)` that takes a list of dictionaries (each with "name" and "age" keys) and returns a pretty-printed JSON string with `indent=2`.
test_suite:
import json

def test_three_friends():
    friends = [
        {"name": "Alice", "age": 25},
        {"name": "Bob", "age": 30},
        {"name": "Charlie", "age": 35}
    ]
    result = exercise.friends_to_json(friends)
    parsed = json.loads(result)
    assert len(parsed) == 3, f"Expected 3 friends, got {len(parsed)}"
    assert parsed[0]["name"] == "Alice", f"Expected first friend Alice, got {parsed[0]['name']!r}"
    assert result.count("\n") >= 3, f"Expected pretty-printed JSON (with newlines), got {result!r}"

def test_single_friend():
    friends = [
        {"name": "Diana", "age": 28}
    ]
    result = exercise.friends_to_json(friends)
    parsed = json.loads(result)
    assert len(parsed) == 1, f"Expected 1 friend, got {len(parsed)}"
    assert parsed[0]["name"] == "Diana", f"Expected name Diana, got {parsed[0]['name']!r}"

def test_empty_list():
    result = exercise.friends_to_json([])
    parsed = json.loads(result)
    assert parsed == [], f"Expected empty list, got {parsed!r}"
